{{nihongo|'''Oshaku Shrine'''|御笏神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

'''Oshaku Shrine''' (おしゃくじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Miyake, Tokyo|Q1154797|qid=Q1154797}}, {{ill|Tokyo|Q1490|qid=Q1490}}.

=== History ===
Its founding period is unknown. However, because it is identified with the {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} '''Sakitamahime-no-Mikoto Shrine''' listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}, it is presumed to have already existed at least during the {{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325}} era ({{ill|901|Q23580|qid=Q23580}}–{{ill|923|Q30108|qid=Q30108}})<ref name="散歩">Tokyo Historical Education Research Society (ed.), ''Historical Walks of Tokyo, Lower Volume (Historical Walks 13): Tama and Islands'', Yamakawa Shuppansha, 2005, p.246.</ref>.

The shrine priests of this shrine have been inherited for generations by the {{ill|Mibushi|Q11429506|qid=Q11429506}}. The Mibu clan is known as the family that compiled the ''{{ill|Miyake-ki|Q17215100|qid=Q17215100}}'', which records the origins of the {{ill|Izu Islands|Q864302|qid=Q864302}}.

The shrine has many merged shrines, including several shikinaisha. In addition to the annual grand festival on October 10, in mid-July the Gozu Tennō Festival (so-called {{ill|Gion Matsuri|Q979873|qid=Q979873}}), derived from one merged shrine, {{ill|Gozu Tennō|Q11570247|qid=Q11570247}} Shrine, is also held lively<ref name="official"/><ref name="kanko">[https://www.miyakejima.gr.jp/see/osyakujinja/ Oshaku Shrine] - Miyakejima Tourism Association</ref><ref name="miyake">[https://www.soumu.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/14miyake/miyakehp/kankousasshi_0503.pdf Miyakejima (pp.66-68, p.84)] - Tokyo Metropolitan Government / Miyakejima Tourism Association</ref>.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* Sakitamahime-no-Mikoto (さきたまひめのみこと) - one of the consort deities of {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Kami}} (Mishima Daimyōjin).

According to the mythology in ''Miyake-ki'', the three sister consorts of Mishima Daimyōjin (Kotoshironushi-no-Kami), worshiped at shrines on Miyakejima, were daughters of an old couple living around {{ill|Hakone|Q11603342|qid=Q11603342}} and {{ill|Lake Ashi|Q187053|qid=Q187053}}, rescued from a dragon (great serpent) and brought to Miyakejima. The eldest is Igamuhime-no-Mikoto at {{ill|Kisaki Shrine|Q134930558|qid=Q134930558|lt=Kisaki Shrine}}, the second is Iwanohime-no-Mikoto at {{ill|Ninomiya Shrine (Q134930277)|ja|二宮神社 (三宅村)|qid=Q134930277|lt=Ninomiya Shrine}}, and the third is Sakitamahime-no-Mikoto at Oshaku Shrine<ref name="chosa-miyake">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz149900-01.html Shrines of Miyakejima] - Survey of Engishiki Shrines</ref>.

=== Cultural properties ===
